facts.en: Its German name, Vierwaldstättersee, means the lake of the four forest cantons: Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne.
The Rütli meadow on its shore is the traditional founding place of the Swiss Confederation.
The lake has several arms, so a boat from Luzern to Flüelen changes direction again and again.
It is shared by Switzerland and France, and is one of the largest lakes in Western Europe.
The Rhône flows in at the eastern end and leaves the lake in Geneva.
Chillon Castle stands on a rock at the water's edge near Montreux.
The lake is long and narrow: about 40 km from end to end and only about 3 km wide.
Its water leaves through the Limmat, in the middle of the city of Zurich.
Ufenau and Lützelau are its two islands, near Rapperswil.
The lake lies in three cantons: Zug, Schwyz and Lucerne.
The Rigi rises directly from its southern shore.
The river Lorze flows both into and out of the lake.
The Aare flows in from Lake Brienz and leaves the lake at Thun.
The lake lies entirely in the canton of Bern, at the foot of the Bernese Alps.
Thun and Spiez are its main towns.
For its size it is very deep: 260 m at the deepest point.
Rivers from the glaciers carry fine rock flour into it, which gives the water its turquoise colour.
The Giessbach falls drop towards the lake on its southern shore.
It is the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland.
Canals link it to Lake Biel and Lake Murten, so boats pass between the three lakes.
Neuchâtel, Yverdon-les-Bains and Estavayer-le-Lac lie on its shores.
St. Peter's Island, where Jean-Jacques Rousseau stayed in 1765, is its best-known place.
The lake lies on the language border: German is spoken on one side, French on the other.
Vineyards cover the northern shore between Biel/Bienne and La Neuveville.
It is the smallest of the three lakes at the foot of the Jura.
The Broye canal links it to Lake Neuchâtel.
The walled medieval town of Murten gives the lake its name.
Three countries share the lake: Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
The Rhine flows in near Bregenz and leaves the lake again on its way to the Rhine Falls.
Mainau, Reichenau and Lindau are its best-known islands.
The lake winds between Switzerland and Italy.
Campione d'Italia, on its shore, is Italian territory surrounded by Switzerland.
A causeway at Melide carries the road and the railway across the lake.
Its shore, at 193 m above sea level, is the lowest point in Switzerland.
Only the northern end is Swiss; most of the lake lies in Italy.
The Brissago Islands, near the Swiss shore, hold a botanical garden.
